items.snippet: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

items.headline: What is holding back Cyprus's Schengen ambitions?
items.snippet: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.

items.headline: New report shows US chip industry's reliance on China
items.snippet: More than 5% of equipment and materials supplied to US chipmakers originate in China, which also possesses some 90% of the rare earths required to manufacture semiconductors.

items.headline: Meta has reached AI ‘frontier,’ Zuckerberg says
items.snippet: Mark Zuckerberg said Meta had reached the “frontier” of AI capabilities with the release of its latest Muse model.

items.headline: Trump faces Russia diesel deal blowback
items.snippet: The US president defended his deal with Moscow to suspend export sanctions on Russian fuel, calling it “the right choice.”

items.headline: Saudi minister says kingdom is fearless after deadly Houthi strikes
items.snippet: Back-to-back Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s airport have threatened the kingdom’s economic ambitions.

items.headline: Cyberattack destroys food at hundreds of French grocery stores
items.snippet: A cyberattack affected at least 400 French supermarkets overnight, raising refrigerator temperatures to more than 122°F (50°C) in some cases.

items.headline: UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
items.snippet: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.

items.headline: Poland reports arrests of 2 Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with Starlink station fire last month
items.snippet: Polish authorities have reported the arrests of two Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."

items.headline: Germany: Labor Minister's resignation puts a spotlight on cracks within the government
items.snippet: Following the sudden resignation of Bärbel Bas as Labor Minister and co-chair of the Social Democratic Party, accusations are flying in Chancellor Merz's coalition government.

items.headline: A charming and 'instructive' dispatch from Rome
items.snippet: This memoir from The New York Times’ former Rome bureau chief explores how Italy’s problems previewed those of the rest of the industrial world.

items.headline: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
items.snippet: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

items.headline: Democrats are making corruption messaging a pocketbook issue
items.snippet: Running against corruption is not new. But Democrats have turned the familiar attack into a broader message tied to voters’ economic pain.

items.headline: OPay readies $4B New York IPO
items.snippet: The fintech firm has seen its lending business overtake payments as its revenue more than doubled in the first half of the year.

items.headline: Ecobank agrees to join Chinese payment platform

items.headline: Mercenaries suffer losses in DR Congo
items.snippet: A battlefield clash highlights the role of US private security contractor Erik Prince as his country seeks greater access to minerals.

items.headline: Saudi plans to expand oil export routes to cut Hormuz reliance
items.snippet: The urgency is growing as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine strain global oil supplies.

items.headline: Mubadala doubles down on Asia investments
items.snippet: The $385 billion Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund is looking to boost investments in China, India, Japan, and South Korea.

items.headline: Israel mints tech unicorns. Can it keep them from leaving for New York?
items.snippet: Tel Aviv Stock Exchange’s pitch is aided by US investors’ preference for AI giants: “New York is no longer an option.”

items.headline: Saudi Arabia’s resolve, and fears of a ‘forever war’
items.snippet: Deadly airport strikes have more Saudis worried how hard the kingdom will be hit.

items.headline: US, European yields unlikely to fall soon, economists say
items.snippet: Experts projected that US 10-year Treasury yields would decline only slightly from current levels to end the year at 5.1%, and would dip to around 4.8% 12 months later.

items.headline: Riyadh hit by deadly Houthi attacks again over the weekend
items.snippet: Several major energy CEOs cancelled travel to Saudi Arabia, which had been preparing several major conferences courting foreign investment.

items.headline: Global oil buffers weaken as global conflict expands
items.snippet: Goldman Sachs over the weekend raised its forecast for average year-end oil prices, warning of “the high sensitivity of interest rates to oil prices.”

items.headline: AI infrastructure investments to drive Asia economic boom
items.snippet: JP Morgan said Asia’s expansion was “broadening from an overwhelmingly tech-led export boom towards more balanced growth from tech.”

items.headline: Russia hammers Ukraine despite President Trump's energy ceasefire
items.snippet: Faced with domestic cost-of-living concerns ahead of midterm elections, the US has agreed to import diesel from Russia.

items.headline: MAGA Inc. plots final midterm money moves
items.snippet: The push includes cutting off spending for some House races, piling in money to shore up others and training its focus on key Senate races.

items.headline: Tanzania seeks investment to tackle youth job pressure
items.snippet: Efforts to partner with private companies are part of a bid to create jobs, said the country’s prime minister.

items.headline: Dangote's Kenya refinery triggers political battle
items.snippet: President William Ruto lauds the benefits of this huge investment but opponents see it as part of a pattern of opaque deals.

items.headline: Obama cuts ad in Mississippi Senate race
items.snippet: Democrats are hoping nominee Scott Colom delivers an upset in the deep red state in the November midterm elections.

items.headline: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
items.snippet: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.

items.headline: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
items.snippet: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?

items.headline: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
items.snippet: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.

items.headline: Fox stays positive on data centers even as public backlash grows
items.snippet: More than half of the references to data centers on Fox News over the last two years would have left viewers with a favorable impression, according to a Semafor analysis.

items.headline: Hack reveals Netanyahu campaign's media ties
items.snippet: The latest breach comes from the Whatsapp account of Netanyahu aide Jonatan Urich.

items.headline: ABC News offers contradictory explanation for vanishing Anduril story
items.snippet: Emails between ABC News and its subjects, provided to Semafor, show the network seeking to downplay its errors by misrepresenting its own processes.

items.headline: China, EU reach agreement to reduce Chinese hybrid vehicle imports
items.snippet: The EU and China reached a deal Friday to reduce China’s shipments of hybrid vehicles to Europe by half.

items.headline: Europe pledges support for Ukraine as rift with US widens
items.snippet: European leaders rushed to back Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy over the weekend amid a widening rift with the US, though the continent’s support for Kyiv may have an expiration date.

items.headline: Data centers emerge as attractive targets in war
items.snippet: Russia and Ukraine have traded strikes on digital infrastructure in recent weeks, triggering major outages on both sides.

items.headline: US threatens to halt Ukraine arms
items.snippet: The US threatened to halt arms sales to Europe for use in Ukraine unless Kyiv stopped striking Russian refineries, the Financial Times reported, accelerating a stunning deterioration in ties between the allies.

items.headline: Thousands detained in India in massive anti-government protests
items.snippet: Indian authorities released the leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party on Sunday, after security forces detained thousands of protesters during massive anti-government demonstrations.

items.headline: Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
items.snippet: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

items.headline: German 'lawfare': When lawsuits become a political weapon

items.headline: Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
items.snippet: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.

items.headline: Georgia's surrogacy industry is booming, but at what cost?
items.snippet: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

items.headline: Germany's population is shrinking, but not everywhere
items.snippet: By 2045, Germany will have more older people, fewer workers and a smaller population overall. Yet some regions will defy this trend. Their success depends on how much they have to offer.
